sentences.en: If you can imagine it, there was a time before time.
sentences.zh: 如果你能想象的话，在时间出现之前，曾有过一段时光。

sentences.en: Well, before clock time, that is.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在钟表时间出现之前。

sentences.en: In fact, there were many decades in colonial America
sentences.zh: 事实上，在殖民时期的美国，有几十年的时间里，

sentences.en: when most people had no earthly idea what time it was.
sentences.zh: 大多数人根本不知道当时到底是几点。

sentences.en: Most people, when they keep time,
sentences.zh: 大多数人记录时间的方式，

sentences.en: they just stick a stick in the ground and call it noon.
sentences.zh: 就是往地里插根棍子，把它当作正午。

sentences.en: This is Michael Malley, a historian of time.
sentences.zh: 这位是时间历史学家迈克尔·马利。

sentences.en: What are you going to do when it's cloudy?
sentences.zh: 那阴天的时候你该怎么办呢？
嗯，可以参考动物的习性。

sentences.en: You woke up with the rooster and at the end of the day.
sentences.zh: 你随着公鸡打鸣起床，一天结束时也随之休息。

sentences.en: There's a phrase in American vernacular culture,
sentences.zh: 美国民间文化里有一个短语，

sentences.en: Well, the thing is, cows do go back to the barn at a certain time of day.
sentences.zh: 问题是，牛确实会在一天中的某个特定时间回到牛棚。

sentences.en: So they could look outside and see the cows heading home
sentences.zh: 所以人们看到牛群往回走，

sentences.en: and they would know it was time for them to go home.
sentences.zh: 就知道自己也该回家了。

sentences.en: In the 1650s, the first public clocks were installed in Boston, Salem, and New York.
sentences.zh: 17世纪50年代，波士顿、塞勒姆和纽约安装了第一批公共时钟。

sentences.en: And they were all the rage.
New England towns would try to get a clock
sentences.zh: 新英格兰地区的城镇都想拥有一个时钟，

sentences.en: and it was a sign of their kind of legitimacy.
sentences.zh: 这被视为一种合法性的象征。

sentences.en: It would be used to call people to prayer or, you know,
sentences.zh: 它会被用来召集人们祈祷，或者，你知道的，

sentences.en: call people to church or call the meeting.
sentences.zh: 召集人们去教堂或参加会议。

sentences.en: And with this clock tower, suddenly the clock was the center of everything.
sentences.zh: 有了这座钟楼，时钟突然成了万物的中心。

sentences.en: Being in earshot of the town bells marked the borders of civilization.
sentences.zh: 能听到城镇钟声的范围，标志着文明的边界。

sentences.en: If you were out of earshot of the town, you were almost in the wilderness.
sentences.zh: 如果你身处钟声之外，就几乎等同于身处荒野。

sentences.en: Life was becoming organized by the clock.
sentences.zh: 生活开始被时钟所组织。

sentences.en: But for the next 100 years, that clock said something different in every city.
sentences.zh: 但在接下来的100年里，每个城市的时钟所显示的时间都不一样。

sentences.en: Noon was one thing in Boston, another in Providence, a third in New York.
sentences.zh: 波士顿的正午是一个时间，普罗维登斯是另一个，纽约又是第三个。

sentences.en: Fine for a farmer, a nightmare for a railroad running on a schedule.
sentences.zh: 这对农民来说没问题，但对按时刻表运行的铁路来说简直是噩梦。

sentences.en: So in 1883, the railroad barons got together and tamed this chaos,
sentences.zh: 于是，1883年，铁路大亨们聚在一起终结了这种混乱，

sentences.en: carving the country into four standard time zones.
sentences.zh: 将全国划分为四个标准时区。

sentences.en: But for the average American worker, that didn't mean much.
sentences.zh: 但对于普通的美国工人来说，这并没有多大意义。

sentences.en: Especially when your employer could still decide what time it was.
sentences.zh: 尤其是当你的雇主仍然可以决定时间的时候。

sentences.en: The clock calls you to work.
You still had to show up to the factory whenever the boss rang the bell.
sentences.zh: 你仍然必须在老板敲钟时赶到工厂。

sentences.en: But people don't trust that because they feel like it's always being bumped ahead,
sentences.zh: 但人们并不信任那个钟，因为他们觉得时间总是被调快了，

sentences.en: you know, to get people in early.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，为了让人们早点到岗。

sentences.en: Everyone knew the foreman messed with the time to get more work out of you.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道工头会动手脚，好让你多干点活。
他们可以随意更改时间。

sentences.en: They could make it ahead in the morning and behind in the afternoon, right?
sentences.zh: 他们可以早上把时间调快，下午又调慢，对吧？

sentences.en: So you never know if that clock is accurate.
sentences.zh: 所以你永远不知道那个时钟准不准。

sentences.en: And once you got inside, a human being was often the one deciding whether you were actually on time.
sentences.zh: 而且一旦你进了工厂，往往是一个人来决定你是否真的准时。

sentences.en: So if you know Joe, the guy checking you in, if he's your buddy,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你认识负责考勤的乔，如果他是你的哥们儿，

sentences.en: you're going to say, come on, Joe, give me a break.
sentences.zh: 你会说，拜托，乔，通融一下吧。

sentences.en: And he's going to mark you as on time when you're not.
sentences.zh: 即使你迟到了，他也会把你记为准时。

sentences.en: Or, you know, conversely, if Joe is the tool of management and eager to punish people he doesn't like,
sentences.zh: 或者，反过来说，如果乔是管理层的走狗，急于惩罚他不喜欢的人，

sentences.en: he can mark you as late when you're not.
sentences.zh: 即使你没迟到，他也能把你记为迟到。

sentences.en: Everybody, employees and employers alike, thought this messiness of time was being used to cheat them.
sentences.zh: 每个人，无论是员工还是雇主，都认为这种混乱的时间管理被用来欺骗他们。

sentences.en: And into this mess walked an unlikely hero, a man who didn't care much about the factory or power or money.
sentences.zh: 就在这种混乱中，出现了一位意想不到的英雄，一个不太关心工厂、权力和金钱的人。

sentences.en: But the clock he built would do more than solve a workplace dispute.
sentences.zh: 但他制造的时钟所做的，远不止解决职场纠纷那么简单。

sentences.en: It would reorder America's relationship to time itself.
sentences.zh: 它将重塑美国与时间本身的关系。

sentences.en: From 99% Invisible and BBC Studios, this is a history of the United States in 100 Objects.
sentences.zh: 来自《99% Invisible》和BBC Studios，这是《美国100件物品历史》。

sentences.en: Today, the Bundy clock and how the first employee time clock sparked a revolution in workplace surveillance and efficiency.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要讲的是邦迪时钟，以及第一台员工考勤钟如何引发了职场监控和效率的革命。

sentences.en: Reporter Ellie Lightfoot has the story.
sentences.zh: 记者艾莉·莱特富特为您报道。

sentences.en: The name of our unlikely hero, this man who would unwittingly change our relationship to time, he's called Willard Bundy.
sentences.zh: 我们这位意想不到的英雄，这位无意中改变了我们与时间关系的人，名叫威拉德·邦迪。

sentences.en: Willard was born in 1845 and grew up in Auburn, New York, a small but booming factory town in the center of the state.
sentences.zh: 威拉德出生于1845年，在纽约州奥本市长大，那是该州中部一个规模虽小但蓬勃发展的工厂城镇。

sentences.en: As a boy, he was kind of an engineering whiz kid.
sentences.zh: 小时候，他是个工程天才。

sentences.en: He works at the Bundy Museum, which, as you can imagine, is all about Willard Bundy.
sentences.zh: 他在邦迪博物馆工作，你可以想象，那里全是关于威拉德·邦迪的内容。

sentences.en: As a child, he would, like, take apart watches and try to reassemble them.
sentences.zh: 小时候，他会拆开手表，然后试着把它们重新组装起来。

sentences.en: Willard grew up to become a professional watch tinkerer, a jeweler.
sentences.zh: 威拉德长大后成为了一名专业的钟表修理工，一名珠宝商。

sentences.en: Because back then, jewelers weren't just jewelers.
sentences.zh: 因为在那个年代，珠宝商不仅仅是卖珠宝的。

sentences.en: They were the town's authority on time.
sentences.zh: 他们是镇上的时间权威。

sentences.en: It was their responsibility to build these big, accurate clocks and keep them on display in their shop window so that people could visit the window and see what time it was.
sentences.zh: 他们的职责是制造这些大型、精准的时钟，并把它们展示在店窗里，这样人们就可以去查看时间。

sentences.en: And it was this part of the job that Willard loved the moSt.
sentences.zh: 而这正是威拉德最喜欢的工作部分。

sentences.en: He'd spent hours and hours constructing these intricate novelty clocks, like this hulking eight-foot-tall clock that he claimed could keep perfect time for a thousand years.
sentences.zh: 他花了无数个小时来制造这些复杂的创意时钟，比如这个巨大的八英尺高的时钟，他声称它能保持一千年的精准时间。

sentences.en: It had dials for not only hours, minutes, and seconds, but also the day of the week, the date of the month, which particular month it was, and the year for 1,000 years.
sentences.zh: 它不仅有时、分、秒的表盘，还有星期、日期、月份，以及长达1000年的年份显示。

sentences.en: But this clock, which, by the way, he called the Wonderful Clock, wasn't just for telling time.
sentences.zh: 但这个时钟，顺便说一下，他称之为“奇妙时钟”，不仅仅是为了报时。

sentences.en: It had bells and whistles that would chime on the hour every hour.
sentences.zh: 它还有各种铃铛和装置，每个整点都会鸣响。

sentences.en: The thing was essentially a cuckoo clock on steroids.
sentences.zh: 这东西本质上就是一个加强版的布谷鸟钟。

sentences.en: But instead of a bird popping out, Willard constructed this elaborate scene, a kind of mechanical diorama of a working mill.
sentences.zh: 但威拉德没有用跳出来的小鸟，而是构建了一个精致的场景，一种机械化的工厂立体模型。

sentences.en: I think it's a lumber mill, actually.
sentences.zh: 我想那其实是个木材厂。

sentences.en: So the waterfall is transporting little logs to be cut.
sentences.zh: 瀑布把小圆木运送到切割处。

sentences.en: There was also a tiny pond with frogs and turtles and fish of every kind.
sentences.zh: 还有一个小池塘，里面有各种青蛙、乌龟和鱼。

sentences.en: There was a mini steam engine and a boat bobbing in the pond.
sentences.zh: 还有一个微型蒸汽机和一艘在池塘里漂浮的小船。

sentences.en: This clock was so popular, such an oddity, that there actually had to be a police officer out front just kind of keeping the crowd moving along.
sentences.zh: 这个时钟太受欢迎了，简直是个奇观，以至于必须派一名警察在前面维持秩序，让围观人群流动起来。

sentences.en: Because people were so enchanted by it that they would just loiter in front of his store.
sentences.zh: 因为人们被它深深吸引，总是在他的店前徘徊。

sentences.en: Willard had wrangled over 3,000 tiny pieces into a kind of masterpiece, which, to me at least, tells me that the man loved order.
sentences.zh: 威拉德将3000多个微小零件拼装成了一件杰作，这至少向我证明，这个人热爱秩序。

sentences.en: So, it's not surprising, really, that he saw the messiness of timekeeping happening in factories across America as a giant problem he needed to solve.
sentences.zh: 所以，他把美国各地工厂里混乱的时间管理视为一个亟待解决的巨大问题，也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: The story goes that one day, Willard walked into a factory in his town and saw how the bosses were keeping track of their employees' time.
sentences.zh: 故事是这样的，有一天，威拉德走进镇上的一家工厂，看到了老板们是如何记录员工时间的。

sentences.en: They assigned each worker one of these little brass discs and expected them to toss it into a bucket every morning to mark themselves present.
sentences.zh: 他们给每个工人发一个小铜牌，要求他们每天早上扔进桶里，以示到岗。

sentences.en: But the system was a mess.
There was no accurate record of when the guy actually showed up.
sentences.zh: 根本没有关于工人到底什么时候到岗的准确记录。

sentences.en: And Willard, he couldn't help himself.
sentences.zh: 威拉德对此实在看不下去了。

sentences.en: He saw a system that existed, but it wasn't up to snuff.
sentences.zh: 他看到了一个现有的系统，但它根本不合格。

sentences.en: So, back in his shop, Willard started building something that was up to snuff.
sentences.zh: 于是，回到店里，威拉德开始制造一些真正合格的东西。

sentences.en: It was basically an ornate wooden box mounted on the wall.
sentences.zh: 它基本上就是一个挂在墙上的华丽木箱。

sentences.en: Kind of like a grandfather clock, except underneath the clock face, there was a little slot for a key.
sentences.zh: 有点像落地钟，只是在钟面下方有一个插钥匙的小槽。

sentences.en: Each worker got their own key.
sentences.zh: 每个工人都有自己的钥匙。

sentences.en: And every morning, when they showed up to work, they'd insert their key into the slot, turn it a quarter turn,
sentences.zh: 每天早上，当他们来上班时，就把钥匙插进槽里，转动四分之一圈，

sentences.en: which would then stamp the exact time they got there onto a ribbon of paper.
sentences.zh: 这就会在纸带上印下他们到达的准确时间。

sentences.en: But after he patented it, Willard wasn't really that into the idea of selling it.
sentences.zh: 但在获得专利后，威拉德对销售它并没有太大兴趣。

sentences.en: Willard was content to stay in his lane, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想威拉德满足于守着自己的一亩三分地。

sentences.en: You know, he wanted to make these very specific objects that brought him joy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他只想制造那些能给他带来快乐的特定物品。

sentences.en: He wasn't necessarily looking to get rich.
He wasn't trying to redefine the system.
sentences.zh: 他也不是想重新定义这个系统。

sentences.en: Maybe Willard wasn't trying to get rich, but his brother was.
sentences.zh: 也许威拉德不想发财，但他弟弟想。

sentences.en: Willard's younger brother, Harlow, is going to play a huge role in the story of the Bundy clock.
sentences.zh: 威拉德的弟弟哈洛，将在邦迪时钟的故事中扮演重要角色。

sentences.en: But Harlow wants things Willard doesn't.
sentences.zh: 但哈洛想要的东西威拉德并不想要。

sentences.en: In fact, the Bundy brothers couldn't have been more different.
sentences.zh: 事实上，邦迪兄弟俩的性格截然不同。

sentences.en: And it's clear our museum man has a favorite.
sentences.zh: 而且很明显，我们的博物馆馆长有偏爱的人。

sentences.en: Everything that we know about Willard tells us that he was a genuinely nice guy.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的关于威拉德的一切都表明，他是个真正的好人。

sentences.en: He was well-liked in the community.
His younger brother, Harlow, was the complete opposite.
sentences.zh: 他的弟弟哈洛则完全相反。

sentences.en: While Willard, the inventor, was a softie.
sentences.zh: 威拉德作为发明家，是个心肠软的人。

sentences.en: Supposedly, he was just like the most romantic man that you can think of.
sentences.zh: 据说，他简直是你所能想象到的最浪漫的人。

sentences.en: He had a very poor reputation throughout town.
Willard was more than happy to spend 20 years making a single clock.
sentences.zh: 威拉德很乐意花20年时间只做一个时钟。

sentences.en: But Harlow, the brother with the business mind, saw the dollar signs almost immediately.
sentences.zh: 但哈洛，那个有商业头脑的弟弟，几乎立刻就看到了商机。

sentences.en: He was aware of what his brother was inventing.
sentences.zh: 他知道他哥哥在发明什么。

sentences.en: He said, hey, if we market these clocks, they're going to sell like hotcakes.
sentences.zh: 他说，嘿，如果我们推销这些时钟，它们一定会卖得非常火爆。

sentences.en: Eventually, Harlow convinces his inventor brother to go into business with him.
sentences.zh: 最终，哈洛说服了他那发明家哥哥与他合伙做生意。

sentences.en: But the Bundy clocks do not immediately sell, like hotcakes.
sentences.zh: 但邦迪时钟并没有立刻卖得火爆。

sentences.en: A lot of business owners didn't necessarily see the need for a time clock like this.
sentences.zh: 很多企业主并不觉得有必要使用这种考勤钟。

sentences.en: A Bundy clock was $75, which I want to say that calculates to about $1,500 to $2,000.
sentences.zh: 一台邦迪时钟要75美元，我想这相当于现在的1500到2000美元左右。

sentences.en: The other problem was that for the first year, they tried to market these clocks directly to workers.
sentences.zh: 另一个问题是，第一年他们试图直接向工人推销这些时钟。

sentences.en: They would take out ads in union magazines or newspapers in factory towns that would read,
sentences.zh: 他们会在工会杂志或工厂城镇的报纸上刊登广告，上面写着：

sentences.en: Hey, factory worker, make sure your boss is paying you correctly.
sentences.zh: “嘿，工厂工人，确保你的老板付给你的工资是正确的。”

sentences.en: Encourage him to buy a Bundy clock.
But this strategy turned out to be a big old flop.
sentences.zh: 但这个策略结果彻底失败了。

sentences.en: If the idea was you get all of your co-workers to rally around this device and tell your boss to buy it,
sentences.zh: 如果你的想法是让所有同事团结起来支持这个设备，并告诉老板去买它，

sentences.en: You know, they're going to do what saves them money.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们只会做那些能省钱的事。

sentences.en: The bosses weren't going to listen to their workers.
sentences.zh: 老板们根本不会听工人的。

sentences.en: So pretty soon, they dump that idea.
sentences.zh: 所以很快，他们就放弃了这个想法。

sentences.en: Someone at the company has the genius idea of flipping the script.
sentences.zh: 公司里有人想出了一个天才的主意，改变了策略。

sentences.en: They put out ads that read,
sentences.zh: 他们刊登了这样的广告：

sentences.en: Hey, factory owners, make sure you aren't being cheated by your lazy, dishonest workers.
sentences.zh: “嘿，工厂老板，确保你没有被懒惰、不诚实的工人欺骗。”

sentences.en: And, you know, then they start selling.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，它们就开始畅销了。

sentences.en: We don't know for certain which brother came up with this,
sentences.zh: 我们不确定是哪个兄弟想出的这个主意，

sentences.en: but in Tom's mind, this is classic Harlow.
sentences.zh: 但在汤姆看来，这绝对是哈洛的典型作风。

sentences.en: I'd like to think Harlow was in charge of the advertisement.
sentences.zh: 我倾向于认为哈洛负责广告宣传。

sentences.en: With everything that we know about his character and demeanor,
sentences.zh: 根据我们对他性格和举止的了解，

sentences.en: a lot of the early ads sound like he wrote them.
sentences.zh: 很多早期的广告听起来就像是他写的。

sentences.en: They were just kind of aggressive.
sentences.zh: 它们显得有点咄咄逼人。

sentences.en: Like, there's this one that's just a giant picture of a bulldog.
sentences.zh: 比如，有一张广告图上画着一只巨大的斗牛犬。

sentences.en: It's the head of a bulldog biting through a time ledger, a timesheet,
sentences.zh: 那是斗牛犬的头，正在咬穿一本考勤账簿，一张考勤表，

sentences.en: Put a watchdog on your payroll.
sentences.zh: 给你的工资单装个看门狗。

sentences.en: This new ad campaign, it works.
sentences.zh: 这个新的广告活动很奏效。

sentences.en: By 1898, they've got 9,000 of their clocks in circulation
sentences.zh: 到1898年，他们已经有9000台时钟在流通，

sentences.en: and are just dominating the market.
But then, around the turn of the century,
sentences.zh: 但后来，在世纪之交前后，

sentences.en: the Bundys joined forces with the makers of the punch clock,
sentences.zh: 邦迪兄弟与打卡钟的制造商联手了，

sentences.en: a new invention where workers wouldn't need to fuss with a key.
sentences.zh: 这是一种新发明，工人不再需要摆弄钥匙。

sentences.en: They could just insert a piece of paper, pull a lever, and stamp it.
sentences.zh: 他们只需插入一张纸，拉动杠杆，就能盖上印章。

sentences.en: And, after Harlow markets the hell out of it,
sentences.zh: 而且，在哈洛极力推销之后，

sentences.en: these clocks actually do sell, like hotcakes.
sentences.zh: 这些时钟真的卖得非常火爆。

sentences.en: And part of the reason that these clocks sell so well
sentences.zh: 这些时钟之所以卖得这么好，部分原因在于

sentences.en: is because they tap into a growing demand.
sentences.zh: 它们迎合了日益增长的需求。

sentences.en: the scale of production is really ramping up.
